newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed Martin to move ahead with THAAD.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed Martin to move ahead with THAAD.

text.p: Despite four test failures, the Pentagon said study teams have recommended that the military continue with Lockheed Martin Corp's development of a key component of the U.S. anti-missile defense program.

The Defense Department said two independent groups of experts concluded that the design and concept are sound for an anti-missile missile being developed by Lockheed Martin for the Theater High-Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) system.

The anti-missile missile failed its fourth flight test in a row March 6, clouding the future of the $17 billion program and showing the technical difficulties of missile defenses launched by former President Ronald Reagan.
The missile, designed to smash into attacking nuclear or other missiles at altitudes up to 50 miles 80 km, failed to hit a test target at White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico.
But the Pentagon said two teams found that "the THAAD design as a hit-to-kill interceptor is sound, as is the concept that THAAD will meet its operational requirements."
